artists.name: Greta Van Fleet
artists.summary: Michigan rock quartet with soaring vocals, guitar-led songs and an elaborate stage aesthetic.

sections.title: Who they are
sections.body: Formed in 2012, the band pairs vocalist Josh Kiszka with guitarist Jake Kiszka, bassist and keyboardist Sam Kiszka, and drummer Danny Wagner. Their sound draws on classic rock; From the Fires won the Grammy for Best Rock Album. They recorded Starcatcher at Nashville’s RCA studios with producer Dave Cobb.

sections.title: Stage style
sections.body: Vogue’s 2023 profile documents custom suits and jumpsuits, embroidery, beads, rhinestones and theatrical makeup, including work with designer Amber Doyle. That describes the performers’ visual world at that time; no audience dress code is established by that article.

sections.title: Nashville listing
sections.body: The Basement East lists October 10 and 17 shows as sold out. Its ticket instructions specify will-call collection and matching purchaser identification; a guest must arrive with the purchaser. Check the official listing for any availability changes.

artists.name: Willi Carlisle
artists.summary: A folksinger whose character-driven songs mix traditional roots, humor and a wide musical range.

sections.title: Sound and stories
sections.body: Carlisle builds songs around people, community and the odd corners of everyday life. His official biography describes an expanding palette that includes old-time, Americana, Cajun music, funk and experimentation. The emphasis is storytelling and folk traditions rather than one fixed acoustic formula.

sections.title: This chapter
sections.body: The Universal Bubba is a 17-track double album made with first-time producer Tyler Childers and his band in a makeshift New Orleans studio. The project gives Carlisle room to change instrumentation and stretch the folk framework. The Nashville tour listing includes Dylan Earl as support.

artists.name: Finn Wolfhard
artists.summary: Canadian actor and musician making scrappy indie rock and power pop.

sections.title: Musical background
sections.body: Wolfhard played in Calpurnia and The Aubreys before his solo work. His 2025 album Happy Birthday favors concise, handmade-sounding guitar songs. Kai Slater contributes production, and the record combines loose garage-band energy with bright power-pop melodies.

sections.title: Starting point
sections.body: Listen to Happy Birthday for the DIY side of his music: intimate textures, rough edges and jangly hooks. The Nashville event is billed as The Common Side Effects Tour with Malcy and is currently labeled sold out by The Basement East.

artists.name: Russian Circles
artists.summary: An instrumental trio moving from patient, spacious passages to dense, heavy guitar music.

sections.title: Who they are
sections.body: Mike Sullivan plays guitar, Dave Turncrantz drums, and Brian Cook bass and keyboards. The Chicago-formed trio writes instrumental music with repetition, gradual builds and sharp changes in weight and volume. Their official biography places them in a broad lineage of heavy rock, progressive music and Midwestern underground bands.

sections.title: What the bill suggests
sections.body: Expect the instruments to carry the narrative: recurring riffs, texture and dynamic shifts take the place of a lead singer. Pelican supports the Nashville show, pairing two Chicago-rooted instrumental bands. The official listing marks this Basement East event 18 and up.

artists.name: Pelican
artists.summary: Chicago instrumental heavy rock shaped by post-hardcore, space rock and melodic guitar interplay.

sections.title: Sound and roots
sections.body: The quartet’s roots include the mixed-genre, all-ages shows at Chicago’s Fireside Bowl. Their own album notes connect the music to post-hardcore, space rock, indie rock and metal. Two guitars weave melodies over bass and drums, with atmosphere and momentum sharing space with the heavy parts.

sections.title: A useful first listen
sections.body: Flickering Resonance, released in 2025, reunited founding guitarist Laurent Schroeder-Lebec with Trevor Shelley de Brauw and brothers Bryan and Larry Herweg. It is a useful entry point to the band’s melodic side. Pelican is the named support act on the Russian Circles Nashville bill.

artists.name: Mind Enterprises
artists.summary: Synth-powered Italo disco with hypnotic rhythms and a deliberately playful retro look.

sections.title: Sound
sections.body: Mind Enterprises is the musical world of Turin-raised producer Andrea Tirone, working with collaborator Roberto Conigliaro. The official biography emphasizes disco basslines, repeating drum patterns and expansive keyboards. The appeal is groove and repetition, with a strong connection to 1980s Italo sounds.

sections.title: Visual aesthetic
sections.body: The act explicitly uses retro athletic clothing, tongue-in-cheek 1980s references and humorous commentary on consumerism. That styling belongs to the performers’ presentation. The source does not establish a dress code for fans. Fred Fancy is the named support on the Nashville listing.

artists.name: Olivia O’Brien
artists.summary: Pop and indie-pop songwriting built around candid emotions and relationships.

sections.title: Musical path
sections.body: O’Brien became widely known through her collaboration with gnash and later songs including Josslyn. Her official biography describes a shift toward a more textured, indie-leaning sound around the 2024 project everywhere i go, there i am. Personal experience and direct emotional writing remain central.

sections.body: The current booking is The PIXIE Tour, with Maya Donovan listed as support. PIXIE is the current album focus on her official site. Her music links are a better guide to the sound than assuming every song follows the style of her early breakout singles.

artists.summary: A Chicago six-piece that adds trumpet and saxophone to upbeat indie and alternative rock.

sections.title: What makes the sound
sections.body: Led by singer and guitarist Axel Ellis, the band brings guitars, bass and drums together with a horn section. Its members met while studying jazz, and formed the group in 2018. The official press biography describes a loose, energetic approach drawing on music across generations.

sections.title: Where to start
sections.body: The album So Much To Tell You and the official Blurry Lights release link provide a starting point for their guitar-and-horns mix. The Nashville date is part of The Late Checkout Tour 2026, with The Hails appearing as the named support act.

artists.name: The Hails
artists.summary: Florida-rooted indie rock with collaborative songwriting and a concept-driven visual identity.

sections.title: Background and sound
sections.body: The band came out of the University of Florida’s college indie scene. Vocalist Robbie Kingsley, guitarist and keyboardist Franco Solari, guitarist Dylan McCue and drummer Zach Levy develop songs together. Their Duckpond material tackles dissatisfaction with work, rising living costs and making a life through art.

sections.title: Visual concept
sections.body: For Duckpond’s videos, the group portrays 1930s bowling-alley pinsetters, tying the visuals to labor and obsolescence. This is an album concept rather than a fan dress rule. The Hails appears on the Ax and the Hatchetmen bill at The Basement East.

artists.summary: New Orleans sludge metal combining heavy riffs, punk abrasion and raw vocals.

sections.title: Sound and history
sections.body: Formed in 1988, EYEHATEGOD is associated with guitarist Jimmy Bower and vocalist Michael IX Williams. sections.body: Cobra lists EYEHATEGOD alongside BLAST!, LUICIDAL and EVIL ARMY for October 7. This is a multi-band heavy-music show, listed as 18 and up. The venue’s exact bill is preserved here; BL’AST! has its own artist profile to keep the support act’s identity distinct.

artists.summary: Santa Cruz hardcore with forceful playing and roots in the 1980s SST scene.

sections.body: The eldest Wooten brother plays guitar and sings. Known as the Teacher, Regi is associated with an unusually broad guitar vocabulary, from chord work and strumming to tapping and percussive slapping. His official family biography places that approach within decades of playing and teaching.

artists.name: Don Aliquo
artists.summary: A Nashville saxophonist, composer and educator with Pittsburgh roots and a broad small-group jazz catalog.

sections.title: Background
sections.body: Aliquo grew up around Pittsburgh jazz, learning from his father, saxophonist Don Aliquo Sr., before building his own performing and recording career. His work includes original compositions, collaborations and small-group recordings. Tenor saxophone and bass clarinet are part of his recorded musical palette.

sections.title: Listening context
sections.body: His catalog bridges jazz tradition and contemporary writing, including the piano-less quartet project Growth. Upcoming bookings include a quartet and a Marc Payne collaboration; check each event’s lineup.

artists.name: Guthrie Trapp
artists.summary: A Nashville guitarist whose instrumental playing crosses country, blues, jazz, rock and soul.

sections.title: Musical background
sections.body: Trapp is a guitarist, composer, session musician and educator. After moving to Nashville, his work included Don Kelley’s band at Robert’s Western World and touring with Patty Loveless and Jerry Douglas. Those connections describe his career, not promised guests at the current show.

sections.title: What to listen for
sections.body: His music draws on country phrasing, blues, jazz, rock, soul and Americana. The guitar moves between those styles rather than staying inside one genre. The 5 Spot explicitly labels the Guthrie Trapp Trio booking as instrumental music; In Stereo is an official release to explore beforehand.

artists.summary: Nashville funk and soul with horns, a hard rhythmic drive and gritty vocals.

sections.body: The official Bandcamp release describes a horn-backed funk group with forceful rhythms and rough-edged vocals. Wrong Step supplies an uptempo, call-and-response entry point; its paired track, Karma Is A Bitch, leans into deep funk. These recordings offer a concrete preview of the band’s musical approach.

sections.title: Local connection
sections.body: The group is based in Nashville and has releases associated with Colemine and Money Mouse Records. The 5 Spot lists AJ & The Jiggawatts by name. The artwork here is the actual Bandcamp single image; no custom show flyer was verified for that booking.
